reaction.episode: CORRECTION episode, data fresh through Oct 30: SPX 7,580.07, -3.37% from its 120-day high, -1.52% below the 50-day but still +3.7% above the 200-day; SMH 522.49, -22.2% from its high after a -6.98% day and sitting between zones; NVDA 204.64 inside Zone 1 (200-210); VIX 19.42, up 12.9% on the day; HY OAS 3.23, calm; mechanical capitulation tally 2 of 4 (zone occupancy and credit calm confirmed; volume climax reversal and VIX rollover not confirmed).
reaction.invalidation: A close above the failure zone (SPX above 7,820 / SMH above 600) with credit calm voids the correction stance and this ladder; conversely a credit break (HY OAS above 4%) voids the buy-the-zone plan entirely.

ladder.response: Tranche A preparation: re-run the capitulation tally; deploy the first 25% only if the tally reaches 3+ and credit stays calm (HY OAS below 4%).
ladder.trigger: SMH closes in Zone 2 (470-505) or NVDA closes in Zone 2 (175-185)

ladder.response: Trap case: no chasing, no adds; treat the bounce as a sell/shrink window for weak holdings, not a re-entry.
ladder.trigger: SMH or SPX bounces into the failure zone (SMH 580-600 / SPX 7,750-7,820) and stalls or rejects

ladder.response: Stand down: all tranche preparation pauses, new money stays 100% in bills, and the ladder is re-audited before any deployment.
ladder.trigger: HY OAS closes above 4% or VIX closes above 25

ladder.response: Tranche A fires: 25% into the Zone 2 names per the approved deployment ladder.
ladder.trigger: Zone 2 print plus tally at 3+ with either a VIX rollover from its 5-day high or an SMH volume-climax reversal

reaction.trapRisk: The first bounce is the trap: SMH fell 6.98% in a day on 1.99x average volume with the close in only 46% of its range — no climax reversal yet — so any rally into SMH 580-600 / SPX 7,750-7,820 that fails there confirms the pivot-and-fail pattern. Entries wait for the failure-zone verdict or a Zone 2 print; never chase the first green day.

strategyPosture: Watch. The correction is active, the AI complex is only partway into its buy zones (NVDA in Zone 1, SMH between zones), and the mechanical capitulation tally is 2 of 4 with neither confirming signal printed — so new money stays 100% in bills under the approved ladder until a Zone 2 print plus tally confirmation fires Tranche A.

themes.counterRead: The divergence is real and worth tracking even though the classification is rotation: credit conditions can flip, and a rotation that keeps grinding the index's largest weights down eventually becomes the rollover it is not yet. The read holds only while lending stays loose and SPX holds above its 200-day.
themes.dataAnchor: The weakness is concentrated, not broad: Mag7 names sit 16% below their 52-week highs on average versus 3.3% for SPY, a 12.7-point divergence gap, with GOOGL weakest at -31.5% and AAPL strongest at -2%. SPX itself is only -3.37% from its 120-day high and still +3.7% above its 200-day (7,309.76). Bank lending standards are LOOSE (SLOOS 0%, far below the ~40% stress threshold), which historically reads as leadership rotation, not a confirmed broad rollover.
themes.label: Rotation, not rollover — index calm masks concentrated Mag7 weakness
themes.narrative: The tape reads as a broad selloff: SPY fell 1.59% on the day and QQQ 3.16%, with the Mag7 leading the decline and the market narrative leaning toward a general rollover.
themes.watchFor: SPX close below its 200-day at 7,309.76 or SLOOS tightening toward 40% would reclassify this from rotation to rollover.

themes.counterRead: Data ahead of price is only an opportunity if a floor forms — none has: SMH closed between zones at 522.49, below its Zone 1 floor of 540, and Friday's low undercut the prior day's. The opportunity names (NVDA score 83, AVGO score 80-81, tier A) are watchlist-grade until the zone and tally conditions in the reaction ladder are met; buying the derating early is catching a falling multiple.
themes.dataAnchor: SMH is -22.23% from its 120-day high and -17.14% over 20 days; NVDA is -15.9% from its high and -11.09% over one month, flagged MULTIPLE_COMPRESSION, with revenue still growing 61.4% YoY. AVGO is -34.1% from its high while revenue grows 55% YoY at a 67.8% gross margin and 42.1% FCF margin. LRCX is -45.5% from its high with revenue growing 131.3% YoY. MU is -29.5% from its high on an acute catalyst but still prints 884.74, above its 700-745 Zone 2. The dislocation is derating, not a demand collapse.
themes.label: AI semis: multiples compressing while revenues still grow
themes.narrative: The AI trade is now priced as a financing trade that cannot bottom until the funding channel clears — semis are treated as the epicenter of the unwind, with SMH down 6.98% in a single day.
themes.watchFor: NVDA holding Zone 1 (200-210) versus sliding into Zone 2 (175-185), and SMH closing into Zone 2 (470-505).

themes.counterRead: Narrative ahead cuts both ways: the unwind is the correction of an overrun story, not evidence the power-demand thesis is false. VST's relative stability and insider buying argue the theme survives in its strongest name while the speculative tail (OKLO, SMR) keeps washing out. Do not buy the theme; if anything, the VST-vs-OKLO split is the selection signal.
themes.dataAnchor: The unwind is the sharpest in the tracked universe over one month: OKLO -30.02%, SMR -27.73%, URA -14.12%, GEV -12.87%, CCJ -10.21% (down 7.84% on the day). VST, a holding, is -29.7% from its high but only -1% over one month — the resilient outlier — and insiders bought $1.17M at the trough. No revenue-growth anchor comparable to the semis is cited for the nuclear names in the input; the move is sentiment and multiple, not a reported demand break.
themes.label: Nuclear / AI power: the purest narrative trade unwinding fastest
themes.narrative: The nuclear-power-for-AI story ran as the cleanest second-order AI play, priced on future power demand from data centers rather than current earnings.
themes.watchFor: VST holding above its recent range while OKLO/SMR keep making new lows would confirm selection over theme; a VST break with the group ends the resilient-name read.

themes.counterRead: Oversold is not a floor — RSI 17.5-27 names can stay oversold while the narrative runs, and the single high-materiality news item in the input (TMDX's earnings and revenue miss) shows misses are still being punished. The DATA_AHEAD read applies to the growing names (DDOG, APP) on a watchlist basis, not as a blanket software buy; the group needs a sentiment turn, not just cheap RSI.
themes.dataAnchor: The declines are deep and sentiment-flagged: RDDT -65.2% from its high with RSI 17.5 and -38.7% over one month, APP -69% with RSI 25, NOW -43% with RSI 26.9, SNOW -20.4%, NET -24.2%, MDB -25.4%. But the fundamentals in the input still grow: DDOG revenue +27.7% YoY at an 80% gross margin, APP +16.4% YoY at a 76% gross margin with a 60.8% FCF margin. The gap between price and reported growth is the widest in the tracked universe.
themes.label: Software / SaaS washout: sentiment-driven, deeply oversold, still growing
themes.narrative: Software is priced as the AI loser — the story that AI eats SaaS has driven a broad, indiscriminate selloff across the group.
themes.watchFor: DDOG or APP printing a higher low with RSI turning up from sub-30, or a software earnings beat that the tape rewards instead of selling.

themes.counterRead: Orderly today is not a guarantee: the 10-year sits at 4.93% with the mechanism behind the move unresolved in this input, and a credit break would change the regime faster than equities can reprice. The calm is a condition to monitor, not a reason to add risk.
themes.dataAnchor: Credit is not cracking: HY OAS is 3.23, below the 4% stand-down line and flagged calm. The curve is positively sloped (2s10s +0.16) with the 10-year at 4.93%, the 2-year at 4.77% and the 30-year at 5.31%; the real 10-year is 2.58% and breakeven inflation 2.35%. VIX is 19.42 — elevated and at its 5-day high, but below the 25 stand-down threshold and not rolling over. Rates and credit agree this is an equity-multiple correction, not a funding event.
themes.label: Credit and rates: orderly correction, not a stress event
themes.narrative: Risk-off tape with VIX spiking 12.91% on the day reads as the start of a stress episode, with the Oct 27-28 FOMC in the active-event set and the Nov 3 midterms on watch.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS closing above 4% or VIX closing above 25 would break the orderly read and trigger stand-down.

watchFor: SMH close into Zone 2 (470-505) or NVDA close into Zone 2 (175-185) — the Tranche A trigger
HY OAS closing above 4% or VIX closing above 25 — the stand-down / regime-break line
SPX close below its 200-day at 7,309.76 — the rotation-to-rollover reclassification
SMH/NVDA bounce into the failure zone (SMH 580-600 / SPX 7,750-7,820) and whether it holds or fails
VIX rolling over from its 5-day high (19.42) or an SMH volume-climax reversal — the two unconfirmed tally signals
whereWaveBuilds: The next move is at the zone boundary: either SMH slides into Zone 2 (470-505) and NVDA into Zone 2 (175-185), which arms the Tranche A trigger, or the tape bounces into the failure zone (SMH 580-600 / SPX 7,750-7,820) and the trap case gets its verdict — with the Nov 3 midterms as the next scheduled catalyst in the event set.
